questions.prompt: Complete this general truth: "Hard training ___ champions in every sport."
questions.explanation: A general truth is true yesterday, today and tomorrow, so it takes the present simple; the subject "Hard training" is singular, so the verb is "makes". "made" and "has made" turn a permanent truth into a past event, and "have made" does not agree with a singular subject.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Karim ___ his old motorbike last winter."
questions.explanation: "last winter" names the moment, and a stated past time forces the simple past, so the irregular form of sell is "sold". "has sold" is the present perfect, which never accepts a stated past time; "sells" is the present; and "selled" adds -ed to a verb that is irregular.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Sami and I ___ each other since our first year at school."
questions.explanation: "since our first year at school" gives a starting point that reaches today, so the sentence needs the present perfect, and the third form of know gives "have known". "knew" is the simple past and stops in the past, "have knew" puts a simple past after have, and "have knowed" invents a regular form for an irregular verb.

questions.prompt: Complete: "The builders haven't finished the roof ___."
questions.explanation: The marker that closes a negative sentence is "yet", and it is used only in negatives and questions, so the sentence ends on yet: the builders haven't finished the roof yet. "ever" and "just" stand between have/has and the participle, never at the end, and "since" must be followed by a starting point such as a date.

questions.prompt: Complete: "My aunt has had the same car ___ nine years."
questions.explanation: "nine years" is a length of time, and a length of time takes "for": for nine years. "since" introduces a starting point such as 2010 or Monday, not a duration, while "from" and "during" cannot open a period that runs up to today with the present perfect.
